title: Cowboys WR George Pickens will be only player to play 2026 on franchise tag
content:
The NFL’s deadline for franchise-tagged players to sign multiyear extensions passed at 4 p.m. ET on Wednesday. As expected, wide receiver George Pickens did not reach an agreement on a long-term deal with the Dallas Cowboys.

Instead, he will play out the 2026 season on the franchise tag before becoming an unrestricted free agent in 2027.

New York Jets running back Breece Hall, Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts and Pickens were the three players franchise-tagged this offseason, while the Indianapolis Colts placed the transition tag on quarterback Daniel Jones. Two weeks later, the Colts signed Jones to a two-year extension in March. Hall signed his extension in May, while Pitts signed his three-year extension in late June.

The Cowboys tagged Pickens after he delivered an All-Pro season in his first year in Dallas, which included 73 receptions, a team-leading 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns.

After some ambiguity during the first part of the offseason, the Cowboys were explicit in April that talks of an extension with Pickens would not linger throughout the offseason and into training camp. Those talks had lingered in recent years with wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, quarterback Dak Prescott and linebacker Micah Parsons.

“We’ve made a decision that we’re going to have George play under the franchise tag, which won’t be a first for us,” Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said in April. “So, there won’t be negotiations on a long-term deal. But that’s certainly not a first for this organization and certainly won’t be a first in the league in terms of this decision as we move forward.”

Pickens signed the franchise tag a few days after Jones’ comments and chose to skip Dallas’ voluntary minicamp, which he said he did upon advice from his agent, David Mulugheta. Pickens showed up for mandatory minicamp in mid-June and said he does not plan to hold out of training camp, which begins July 29 in Oxnard, Calif.

“What’s important to me is winning,” Pickens said. “Like I said from the beginning, I always wanna bring a Super Bowl to a group of guys that never had that feeling. That’s really the most important part to me.”

Looking to the future, the Cowboys can place the franchise tag on Pickens again in 2027, but it would be costly. Teams that use the franchise tag on a player for a second consecutive season must either pay the player that year’s tag amount for his position or 120 percent of his prior year’s salary, whichever figure is higher.

Pickens will make $27.3 million playing on the tag in 2026, so his franchise tag figure for 2027 would hover around $33 million. That salary would be fully guaranteed and hit the Cowboys’ cap in its entirety in 2027, making it an unlikely scenario. In terms of average annual value, $33 million would make Pickens the sixth-highest-paid receiver in the league, tied with Pittsburgh’s DK Metcalf, and just $1 million behind Lamb.

In all likelihood, Pickens will enter 2027 as an unrestricted free agent and sign a new contract, whether that be in Dallas or somewhere else.
